To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the norm of the difference between the values of an integrable function f and the corresponding values obtained by a cubature formula with a given lattice is of order O (n − 1 / 4 ), where n is the number of nodes.

the rate of convergence for the norm of the cubature error on a Banach space with a weight function in the Bessel scale is determined by the rate of convergence of the Fourier coefficients of the error.

the norm of the cubature error is bounded by the norm of the difference of the function and its projection on the space of functions with a given lattice and by a factor that decreases with the number of nodes as the inverse of a power of the number of nodes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the rate with which cubature formulas converge on the spaces of periodic and aperiodic functions with respect to the norm of a given Banach space.
the rate of convergence for cubature formulas with nodes from the lattices of the form hHγ.
the rate of convergence of cubature formulas with nodes from a lattice and with equidistributed points.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rate of convergence of cubature formulas on the space of periodic functions with weight is determined by the order of the weight, whereas for the aperiodic case the convergence depends on the smoothness of the weight.

for the cubature formulas with equidistributed and with hHγ nodes the rate of convergence is the same, and the same is true for the formulas with the nodes from the lattice of the type hHγ and with the nodes equidistributed on the lattice hHγ.
for the cubature formulas with nodes from a lattice hHγ, the rate of convergence in strong norm is equal to the rate of convergence of the corresponding Fourier series.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we establish a general theory of convergence of cubature formulas on the space of periodic functions and aperiodic functions.

we have found the exact rates of convergence for the cubature formulas with equidistributed and hHγ nodes in all the spaces mentioned above, and for all the spaces of aperiodic and periodic functions with weight in Bessel and Gelfand scales.
in the current chapter we establish estimates for the norms in the spaces of periodic functions with the weight in the Bessel scales, and also in the L 1 and L 2 spaces of aperiodic integrands.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rate of strong convergence of the cubature formulas hHγ and of the formulas with equidistributed points is the same as the rate of convergence of the best approximants from the linear subspace spanned by the first N+1 functions in a Bessel basis.
the convergence rates are the same for all the formulas with the same number of nodes, regardless of whether these nodes are equidistributed or not.
, in contrast to the classical theory of cubature formulas, the rates of strong convergence of formulas with equidistributed and hHγ nodes are the same.
